items.readable_text:
Content:
Remember that a unit fraction is a fraction containing [MATH: {\color{blue}{1}}] in the numerator. So, for example, the fractions

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}{1}}2, \qquad\dfrac{\color{blue}{1}}{12}]
are both unit fractions, whereas

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}{2}}9, \qquad \dfrac{\color{red}{3}}{5}]
are not unit fractions

Content:
In this lesson, we will use models to divide unit fractions by whole numbers.

Content:
Let's use a fraction model to find the value of

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{2} \div 2.]
We start with a square model of [MATH: \dfrac12,] split vertically.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/eb1a91fcfd1b9a74da63287a81efb536]

Content:
To divide [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}] by [MATH: {\color{blue}2},] we split the above whole into [MATH: \color{blue}2] equal parts horizontally. Then, we remove any shaded parts that are not in the bottom row.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e432923955052291e5155981220727f4]

Content:
From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents [MATH: \dfrac{1}{4}] of the whole.

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{2} \div 2 = \dfrac{1}{4}.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Remember that a unit fraction is a fraction containing [MATH: {\color{blue}{1}}] in the numerator. So, for example, the fractions

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}{1}}2, \qquad\dfrac{\color{blue}{1}}{12}]
are both unit fractions, whereas

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}{2}}9, \qquad \dfrac{\color{red}{3}}{5}]
are not unit fractions

Content:
In this lesson, we will use models to divide unit fractions by whole numbers.

Content:
Let's use a fraction model to find the value of

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{2} \div 2.]
We start with a square model of [MATH: \dfrac12,] split vertically.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/eb1a91fcfd1b9a74da63287a81efb536]

Content:
To divide [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}] by [MATH: {\color{blue}2},] we split the above whole into [MATH: \color{blue}2] equal parts horizontally. Then, we remove any shaded parts that are not in the bottom row.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e432923955052291e5155981220727f4]

Content:
From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents [MATH: \dfrac{1}{4}] of the whole.

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{2} \div 2 = \dfrac{1}{4}.]
